title: Region-aware node decommissioning & tamper-evident retention ledger
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Customers running Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) require provable guarantees when a node or rack is decommissioned (planned or emergency). Current tools produce ad-hoc logs and snapshots that are hard to correlate with retention policies and residency constraints. This ticket implements a region-aware decommission orchestration flow plus a tamper-evident retention ledger that bundles cryptographically-signed evidence for compliance audits.

Goals:
- Prevent accidental movement of region-bound data during decommission or lifecycle operations.
- Enforce per-customer retention settings at decommission time and produce a compact, signed evidence bundle suitable for auditors.
- Gate regional failover/fallback (temporary evacuation lanes) until proof-of-retain/erase checks complete for affected resources.
- Make evidence generation automated and machine-readable to integrate with Compliance Console and support incident postmortems.

Scope (what's in):
- Decommission orchestration workflow for Private deployments (VPC and on-prem) that marks nodes as STAGED_DECOMMISSION -> READONLY -> SNAPSHOT -> ERASE/RELOCATE as applicable.
- Retention ledger service that records retention policy evaluation results and actions; ledger entries are JSON lines signed with cluster KMS key.
- Evidence bundler: produces a per-customer .tar.gz containing signed ledger entries, snapshots (hashes only by default), KMS attestations, and a human-readable summary.
- Integration with failover gating: the regional routing controller will wait for ledger completion or explicit override before promoting fallback lanes.

Out of scope (for this ticket): automated cross-region migration of customer data, UX work in Console (follow-up PM ticket), on-prem hardware decommission procedures beyond orchestration API.
acceptance_criteria: Decommission orchestration API exists and supports the lifecycle: STAGED_DECOMMISSION, READONLY, SNAPSHOT_CREATED, ACTION_COMPLETE.
Ledger entries are written for each lifecycle transition and are signed by the cluster KMS; entries are immutable and exportable per-customer.

Evidence bundler produces a deterministic artifact containing: ledger.jsonl (signed), snapshot-hashes.txt, kms-attestation.txt, and a summary.md; artifact is stored in staging retention for 90 days by default.
Regional routing controller will not perform permanent failover to a non-resident region for a customer until ledger indicates ACTION_COMPLETE or an authorized override is recorded.
Automated tests cover: ledger signing/verification, decommission state transitions, evidence bundler artifact contents, and failover gating behavior in the simulator environment.
Performance: creating evidence bundle for a typical customer (<=500GB, snapshot-hash only) completes under 120s in dedicated environment and under 300s in on-prem tests.
Docs/Runbook: runbook describing manual override steps and how to fetch/verify evidence is checked into Confluence and linked from incident playbooks.
implementation_notes: New microservice: retention-ledger-service (Go), exposes REST endpoint for append/read and an export endpoint that packages evidence bundles.

Data model: flat JSONL entries with fields (timestamp, cluster_id, node_id, customer_id, lifecycle_state, policy_version, action_hash, signature). No customer data is embedded; only snapshot hashes are recorded by default.
Signing: leverage existing KMS integration (private cluster KMS) to produce ECDSA signatures; include kms-key-id in ledger entries for verifiability.
Orchestration hook: serving-runtime will call /decom/v1/start and emit lifecycle events; runtime must pause any cross-region relocation operations when node is STAGED_DECOMMISSION.

Failover gating: routing-controller consults ledger export status for affected customers; fall back to legacy behavior if ledger service is unreachable and safeguards are present (audit log + notify SRE/PM).

Storage: evidence bundles stored in internal artifact storage with access controls; retention policy for evidence bundles defaults to 90 days but is configurable per-customer via Private deployment config.
Compatibility: provide a feature flag to enable the ledger flow per-deployment to allow staged rollouts and compatibility tests with older control planes.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy retention-ledger-service to staging clusters; enable feature flag for 3 pilot customers on dedicated private clusters.
Phase 2 (internal): enable for all internal test tenants and run decommission drills; collect perf metrics and tweak snapshot/hash strategy.
Phase 3 (customer opt-in): offer as opt-in for new Private customers and a small group of existing customers requiring stronger evidence; gather feedback.
Phase 4 (enforced): default-on for new private deployments and offered upgrade path for legacy customers (after 2-week notice and migration runbook).
test_plan: Unit tests for ledger signing and verification (mock KMS).
Integration tests exercising full lifecycle (staged -> readonly -> snapshot -> action_complete) in CI environment with simulated data volumes.
End-to-end test in a private cluster lab: run a scheduled decommission drill with routing-controller and confirm gating behavior blocks cross-region promotion until evidence bundle is present.
Fuzz tests for malformed ledger entries and KMS failures to validate graceful fallback and alerting.
monitoring_and_alerts: SLO: retention-ledger append latency P95 < 250ms in dedicated environment; alert on breach.
Alert if evidence bundle generation fails more than 3 times for the same customer within 24h (PagerDuty to SRE + Notify PM).
Telemetry: counts of STAGED_DECOMMISSION events per region/customer, bundle size distribution, generation latency histogram.
Audit log: every manual override must create an immutable audit record linked to the corresponding ledger entry and be stored for compliance retention window.
